work_protocol.github_change_flow: Prefer connected GitHub connector; read actual current main/target files before modifying. For multi-file changes, create blobs -> tree -> commit -> fast-forward update_ref with expected SHA; then read back to verify.
work_protocol.avoid_codex: Do not delegate to Codex unless explicitly requested; if asked to write Codex tasks, use separate Markdown file for long prompts and recommend reasoning budget.
work_protocol.docs_freeze: Treat README, README.en, public docs, icons and policy as protected. Change them during #syncdocs or when user explicitly directs changes to particular protected files; event ledger is an exception.

work_protocol.document_quality: README targets end users, not chat participant. Avoid personal learning scenarios, AI collaboration notes, tool limitations, internal private paths, passwords, drive IDs, and iOS disclaimers.
work_protocol.code_changes: Do not silently bump version; use v0.5.5 until user approves release. Preserve historical tags and release v0.5.4.

work_protocol.release_workflow: Existing RELEASE.bat/release_history.ps1 is v0.5.4-only; do not repurpose silently. After v0.5.5 docs commit and full Windows test acceptance, create annotated v0.5.5 tag on the docs-sync commit and publish GitHub Release from vguitar/docs/releases/v0.5.5.md with git and gh. Existing tags immutable; no force push. Current GitHub connector may not support Release write actions; use authenticated local CLI.
work_protocol.drive_workflow: Google Drive vGUITAR is a private archive, not the canonical current code. Google Drive folder uses Restricted and Limit access; connector access through owner was verified previously, recheck upon resume. No user data or Drive IDs in GitHub.

shell_block_contract.style_name: vFLOW for WSL; Windows PowerShell for Windows-only operations
shell_block_contract.primary_development_shell_preference: WSL/Bash, when a WSL environment is available; GUI and other native-Windows behavior must execute under Windows Python.
bash_script_style: One complete copy-pasteable Bash code block per scenario.
First command is cd to the actual project root provided by the user; fail if missing.
Use clear -x when interactive terminal cleanliness helps, without destroying scrollback; avoid unconditional clearing in CI/noninteractive sessions.
Check prerequisites and git HEAD/status before stateful operations.
Color-coded, numbered [1/N] stage headers with printf; set -e or explicit traps; print final PASS/FAIL and exit status.
Pause for an explicit READY confirmation via /dev/tty before any destructive or major irreversible local step.
Use real commands and correct quoting; do not invent runner commands or environment activation paths.
Do not feed Windows python.exe the same heredoc stdin as the surrounding Bash script; use </dev/null where necessary.
shell_block_contract.windows_native_execution: Prefer .\RUN.bat for Windows launch; .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe for native tests. Avoid using Linux Python for validating Windows audio behavior.
shell_block_contract.history_specificity: vFLOW conventions are shared user preferences recovered from past projects; do not pretend they were all explicitly defined in the vGUITAR repo. This handoff standardizes them for future vGUITAR responses.

boot_procedure: Read this handoff file from GitHub via connected GitHub plugin (private repository, not public web).
Read repository main metadata and compare observed HEAD to handoff snapshot (this handoff commit itself advances main).
Read VERSION.json, current README.md/README.en.md, vguitar/project_policy.json, vguitar/docs/dev/events.json tail, latest CHANGELOG and directory tree.
Use connected Google Drive to locate folder named vGUITAR; list existing 14 legacy archive/index/preview files, verifying any drift. Do not duplicate these files.

If actual source tests or artifacts are needed, initialize a clean scratch working directory, fetch only missing source files via authorized connectors or use a verified local clone; never assume the local Windows filesystem is mounted in the cloud.
For WSL commands, use the copy-pasteable vFLOW block convention and the local WSL path supplied in bootstrap. Prefer relative paths in files.
Summarize live state, deviations since snapshot, sandbox paths that were truly created, tests actually run, and next safest action.
Do not infer successful tests or releases from intent; honor GitHub docs freeze and user approval gates.
